Designs the node-based network and writes its two GTFS feeds:

1. **Demand grid and p-median nodes** — a half-mile cell grid over Seattle loaded
   with SoundCast/DaySim trip origins and destinations; a p-median model picks 12
   nodes (7 anchored on Link stations).
2. **Rail and express-bus corridors** — the Link and Monorail lines from the
   Spring 2026 feeds, plus express-bus corridors between nodes chosen by an
   integer program; written to `gtfs_node_bus.zip`.
3. **Local feeder routes** — local routes that bring every frequent and local stop
   to a node, chosen by an assignment integer program; written to
   `gtfs_node_local.zip`.

Design tables and shapefiles go to `outputs/node_design/`; the feeds go to
`outputs/gtfs/`.

# Part 1 — Demand grid and p-median nodes

### Goal

Build the inputs for the node-based network design:

1. A regular 0.5 mi × 0.5 mi grid over Seattle (candidate node locations).
2. A demand value per cell = sum of trips that originate or end at a parcel
   in that cell, weighted by `trexpfac`.
3. Select `p_nodes` node locations via p-median, optionally **forcing** a
   set of cell IDs to be in the solution (used to snap nodes onto existing
   Link station cells).

Each PSRC trip contributes up to 2 endpoint-trips to the demand surface
(1 if only one end is in Seattle, 2 if it is wholly intra-Seattle).

### Load parcel geography

Parcel CSV has a WKT `geometry` column in EPSG:2926. We promote to `sf`
and filter to Seattle parcels (cells outside Seattle aren't candidate
node locations).

```{r load-parcels}
parcel_dt <- fread(params$parcel_map_csv)
parcel_dt[, ParcelID := as.character(ParcelID)]

parcel_sf <- st_as_sf(parcel_dt, wkt = "geometry", crs = params$planar_crs)

parcel_seattle_sf <- parcel_sf %>%
  filter(.data[[params$city_col]] == params$seattle_name)

cat("Seattle parcels:", nrow(parcel_seattle_sf), "\n")
```

### Seattle boundary

```{r seattle-boundary}
seattle_place <- tigris::places(state = "WA", year = 2020, class = "sf") %>%
  filter(NAME == params$seattle_name) %>%
  st_transform(params$planar_crs) %>%
  st_union() %>%
  st_make_valid()
```

### Build the cell grid

A regular square grid over the Seattle bbox, then keep only cells that
intersect the city boundary. Cell IDs are sequential and stable for a
given bbox + cellsize.

```{r build-grid}
grid_full <- st_make_grid(
  seattle_place,
  cellsize = params$cell_size_ft,
  square   = TRUE
) %>%
  st_sf(cell_id = seq_along(.))

grid <- grid_full %>%
  filter(lengths(st_intersects(., seattle_place)) > 0)

cat("Cells covering Seattle:", nrow(grid),
    sprintf(" (%.1f mi cellsize)\n", params$cell_size_ft / 5280))
```

### Assign parcels to cells

Spatial join: each Seattle parcel gets the `cell_id` of the cell it falls in.
Points on cell boundaries (rare) can match more than one cell — we keep the first.

```{r parcel-cell-join}
parcel_cell <- parcel_seattle_sf %>%
  st_join(grid, join = st_intersects) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(ParcelID, cell_id) %>%
  filter(!is.na(cell_id)) %>%
  distinct(ParcelID, .keep_all = TRUE)

parcels_per_cell <- parcel_cell %>%
  count(cell_id, name = "n_parcels")

summary(parcels_per_cell$n_parcels)
```

### Aggregate trips to cells

```{r duckdb-trips}
con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = ":memory:")
dbExecute(con, "PRAGMA threads=12;")

dbWriteTable(con, "parcel_cell", parcel_cell, overwrite = TRUE)
dbExecute(con, "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pc_parcelid ON parcel_cell(ParcelID);")

trips_path <- normalizePath(params$trips_tsv, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
trips_rel  <- sprintf(
  "read_csv_auto('%s', delim='\\t', header=true, quote='\"', escape='\"')",
  trips_path
)

wt_col     <- params$trips_weight_col
origin_col <- params$origin_parcel_col
dest_col   <- params$dest_parcel_col

sql_origin <- sprintf("
  SELECT pc.cell_id AS cell_id,
         SUM(COALESCE(CAST(t.%s AS DOUBLE), 0.0)) AS origin_trips
  FROM %s t
  JOIN parcel_cell pc
    ON CAST(t.%s AS VARCHAR) = pc.ParcelID
  GROUP BY 1
", wt_col, trips_rel, origin_col)

sql_dest <- sprintf("
  SELECT pc.cell_id AS cell_id,
         SUM(COALESCE(CAST(t.%s AS DOUBLE), 0.0)) AS dest_trips
  FROM %s t
  JOIN parcel_cell pc
    ON CAST(t.%s AS VARCHAR) = pc.ParcelID
  GROUP BY 1
", wt_col, trips_rel, dest_col)

origin_demand <- dbGetQuery(con, sql_origin)
dest_demand   <- dbGetQuery(con, sql_dest)

dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

cell_demand <- full_join(origin_demand, dest_demand, by = "cell_id") %>%
  mutate(
    origin_trips = coalesce(origin_trips, 0),
    dest_trips   = coalesce(dest_trips,   0),
    total_demand = origin_trips + dest_trips
  )

grid_demand <- grid %>%
  left_join(cell_demand, by = "cell_id") %>%
  mutate(
    origin_trips = coalesce(origin_trips, 0),
    dest_trips   = coalesce(dest_trips,   0),
    total_demand = coalesce(total_demand, 0)
  )

summary(grid_demand$total_demand)
```

### Save the demand grid

```{r save-grid}
saveRDS(
  grid_demand,
  file.path(params$out_dir, sprintf("grid_demand_%dft.rds", params$cell_size_ft))
)
fwrite(
  st_drop_geometry(grid_demand),
  file.path(params$out_dir, sprintf("grid_demand_%dft.csv", params$cell_size_ft))
)
```

## p-median node selection (with optional forced facilities)

We pick `p_nodes` cell locations to act as transit nodes. Some cells may be
**forced** into the solution (passed via `params$forced_cell_ids`) — used
here to snap nodes onto existing Link station cells. The remaining
`p_nodes - length(forced)` facility slots are optimized freely.

- **Demand points** = all cell centroids, weighted by `total_demand`.
- **Candidates for free slots** = all cells *not* already forced.
- **Distance** = Euclidean between centroids (EPSG:2926 → miles).
- **Objective**: minimize Σᵢ wᵢ · dᵢ, where dᵢ is the distance from cell i
  to its nearest selected node.

Solved with a **Teitz–Bart interchange heuristic** that swaps only the
free facility slots; forced slots stay pinned across iterations.

### Inputs

```{r pmedian-inputs}
centroids <- st_centroid(grid_demand)
coords_ft <- st_coordinates(centroids)

D_mi <- as.matrix(dist(coords_ft)) / 5280
w    <- as.numeric(grid_demand$total_demand)
n    <- length(w)

cat(sprintf("Distance matrix: %d x %d cells\n", n, n))
cat(sprintf("Weight range: %s — %s trips\n",
            format(round(min(w)), big.mark = ","),
            format(round(max(w)), big.mark = ",")))
```

### Teitz–Bart heuristic with forced facilities

```{r pmedian-solver}
pmed_cost <- function(facs, D, w) {
  if (length(facs) == 1L) {
    nearest_d <- D[, facs]
  } else {
    nearest_d <- matrixStats::rowMins(D[, facs, drop = FALSE])
  }
  sum(w * nearest_d)
}

# Teitz–Bart interchange, multi-start, with support for forced facilities.
# `forced` is an integer vector of row indices into D (NOT cell_ids).
# Those indices are guaranteed to appear in every candidate solution; only
# the remaining (p - length(forced)) slots are eligible for swaps.
tb_pmedian <- function(D, w, p, forced = integer(0),
                       n_starts = 15, seed = 42, verbose = TRUE) {
  if (!requireNamespace("matrixStats", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Install matrixStats: install.packages('matrixStats')")
  }
  set.seed(seed)
  n <- nrow(D)

  forced <- unique(as.integer(forced))
  if (length(forced) > p) {
    stop(sprintf("Asked for p=%d nodes but %d facilities are forced.",
                 p, length(forced)))
  }
  free_p           <- p - length(forced)
  free_candidates  <- setdiff(seq_len(n), forced)

  if (free_p == 0L) {
    # Edge case: every slot is forced. Just return.
    return(list(facilities = sort(forced),
                cost       = pmed_cost(forced, D, w),
                start      = 0L,
                forced     = forced))
  }

  best <- NULL
  for (s in seq_len(n_starts)) {
    # Weighted random seed for the free slots (high-demand cells more likely)
    init_probs   <- pmax(w[free_candidates], 1e-6)
    free_init    <- sample(free_candidates, free_p, prob = init_probs)
    selected     <- c(forced, free_init)
    cur_cost     <- pmed_cost(selected, D, w)

    # Free slots are positions (length(forced)+1) .. p in `selected`
    free_slots <- seq_len(free_p) + length(forced)

    repeat {
      improved <- FALSE
      for (i_idx in free_slots) {
        for (j in setdiff(free_candidates, selected)) {
          candidate          <- selected
          candidate[i_idx]   <- j
          c_new              <- pmed_cost(candidate, D, w)
          if (c_new < cur_cost - 1e-9) {
            selected <- candidate
            cur_cost <- c_new
            improved <- TRUE
            break
          }
        }
        if (improved) break
      }
      if (!improved) break
    }

    if (is.null(best) || cur_cost < best$cost) {
      best <- list(facilities = sort(selected),
                   cost       = cur_cost,
                   start      = s,
                   forced     = forced)
    }
    if (verbose) {
      cat(sprintf("  start %2d: cost = %s  (best so far: %s)\n",
                  s,
                  format(round(cur_cost), big.mark = ","),
                  format(round(best$cost), big.mark = ",")))
    }
  }
  best
}
```

### Translate forced cell IDs to row indices

The user passes `forced_cell_ids` in terms of `cell_id` (what shows up on
the maps). The optimizer works on row indices in `grid_demand` / `D_mi`,
so we look them up here and bail loudly if any aren't found.

```{r pmedian-forced}
forced_cell_ids <- as.integer(params$forced_cell_ids)
if (length(forced_cell_ids) == 0L) {
  forced_indices <- integer(0)
  cat("No forced cells — running unconstrained p-median.\n")
} else {
  forced_indices <- match(forced_cell_ids, grid_demand$cell_id)
  if (any(is.na(forced_indices))) {
    bad <- forced_cell_ids[is.na(forced_indices)]
    stop("Forced cell_ids not present in grid: ",
         paste(bad, collapse = ", "))
  }
  forced_in_seattle <- grid_demand[forced_indices, ] %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    select(cell_id, origin_trips, dest_trips, total_demand)
  cat(sprintf("Forced %d cells (free slots: %d):\n",
              length(forced_indices), params$p_nodes - length(forced_indices)))
  print(forced_in_seattle)
}
```

### Run

```{r pmedian-run}
t0  <- Sys.time()
res <- tb_pmedian(D_mi, w,
                  p        = params$p_nodes,
                  forced   = forced_indices,
                  n_starts = params$n_starts)
t1  <- Sys.time()

cat(sprintf("\nBest cost: %s demand-miles  (in %.1f s)\n",
            format(round(res$cost), big.mark = ","),
            as.numeric(t1 - t0, units = "secs")))
cat("Best start index:", res$start, "\n")

selected_cell_ids <- grid_demand$cell_id[res$facilities]
forced_cell_ids_chosen <- grid_demand$cell_id[res$forced]

cat("\nForced cell IDs (always in solution):\n")
print(forced_cell_ids_chosen)
cat("\nAll selected cell IDs:\n")
print(selected_cell_ids)
```

### How many nodes? Coverage by node count

The node count was chosen from an unconstrained p-median sweep (no forced
cells): demand-weighted mean distance to the nearest node and the share of
demand within 0.25 and 0.5 miles of a node, for 6 to 16 nodes. Improvement
falls below 10% per step beyond 12 nodes (thesis Table 8).

```{r pmedian-node-count-sweep}
pmed_metrics <- function(facilities, D, w) {
  d <- apply(D[, facilities, drop = FALSE], 1, min)
  c(weighted_avg_mi = sum(w * d) / sum(w),
    pct_within_0_25 = 100 * sum(w * (d <= 0.25)) / sum(w),
    pct_within_0_5  = 100 * sum(w * (d <= 0.5))  / sum(w))
}
sweep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq(6, 16, by = 2), function(p) {
  r <- tb_pmedian(D_mi, w, p = p, n_starts = params$n_starts, verbose = FALSE)
  data.frame(p = p, t(pmed_metrics(r$facilities, D_mi, w)))
}))
fwrite(sweep, file.path(params$out_dir, "pmedian_sensitivity.csv"))
sweep
```

### Assignment of every cell to its nearest node

```{r pmedian-assignment}
D_sub <- D_mi[, res$facilities, drop = FALSE]

nearest_idx <- if (params$p_nodes == 1L) {
  rep(1L, n)
} else {
  max.col(-D_sub, ties.method = "first")
}

nearest_dist_mi <- D_sub[cbind(seq_len(n), nearest_idx)]
nearest_cell_id <- grid_demand$cell_id[res$facilities[nearest_idx]]

grid_demand <- grid_demand %>%
  mutate(
    assigned_node   = nearest_cell_id,
    dist_to_node_mi = nearest_dist_mi,
    is_node         = cell_id %in% selected_cell_ids,
    is_forced_node  = cell_id %in% forced_cell_ids_chosen
  )

weighted_avg_mi <- with(
  grid_demand,
  sum(total_demand * dist_to_node_mi) / sum(total_demand)
)
cat(sprintf("Demand-weighted avg distance to nearest node: %.2f mi\n",
            weighted_avg_mi))
cat(sprintf("Share of demand within 0.5 mi of a node: %.1f%%\n",
            100 * with(grid_demand,
                       sum(total_demand * (dist_to_node_mi <= 0.5)) /
                         sum(total_demand))))
```

### Save results

```{r pmedian-save}
nodes_df <- grid_demand %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(is_node) %>%
  select(cell_id, origin_trips, dest_trips, total_demand, is_forced_node) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_demand))

assignment_df <- grid_demand %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(cell_id, total_demand, assigned_node, dist_to_node_mi,
         is_node, is_forced_node)

saveRDS(
  list(
    p              = params$p_nodes,
    n_forced       = length(forced_indices),
    forced_cell_ids = forced_cell_ids_chosen,
    nodes          = nodes_df,
    assignment     = assignment_df,
    cost           = res$cost,
    metrics        = pmed_metrics(res$facilities, D_mi, w),
    n_starts       = params$n_starts,
    cell_size_ft   = params$cell_size_ft
  ),
  file.path(params$out_dir, sprintf("pmedian_p%d.rds", params$p_nodes))
)

fwrite(nodes_df,
       file.path(params$out_dir,
                 sprintf("pmedian_p%d_nodes.csv", params$p_nodes)))
fwrite(assignment_df,
       file.path(params$out_dir,
                 sprintf("pmedian_p%d_assignment.csv", params$p_nodes)))

nodes_df
```

# Part 2 — Rail and express-bus corridors

### Goal

Identify the **Link corridor** as an ordered sequence of cell IDs (with
interstation travel times in seconds), so step 3 (greedy set cover) can
treat it as a pre-existing line and design the bus corridor set to
**complement** it rather than parallel it.

Outputs of this step: `outputs/node_design/rail_corridors.rds` (ordered cells along
each rail line with interstation travel times), plus `rail_corridor_cells.csv` and
`rail_interstation_times.csv`.

### GTFS helpers

We need to read individual GTFS members without unpacking the whole feed,
since the r5 directory may have multiple agency feeds.

```{r gtfs-helpers}

read_gtfs_member <- function(zipfile, member) {
  members <- tryCatch(utils::unzip(zipfile, list = TRUE)$Name, error = function(e) character())
  if (!(member %in% members)) return(NULL)

  td <- tempfile("gtfs_")
  dir.create(td)
  utils::unzip(zipfile, files = member, exdir = td)
  out <- data.table::fread(file.path(td, member), na.strings = c("", "NA"))
  unlink(td, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
  out
}

active_service_ids <- function(zipfile, service_date) {
  service_date <- as.Date(service_date)
  ymd <- format(service_date, "%Y%m%d")
  dow <- tolower(weekdays(service_date))

  cal  <- read_gtfs_member(zipfile, "calendar.txt")
  cdat <- read_gtfs_member(zipfile, "calendar_dates.txt")

  active <- character()
  if (!is.null(cal) && nrow(cal) > 0) {
    cal <- as.data.table(cal)
    if (dow %in% names(cal)) {
      base_active <- cal[
        get(dow) == 1 &
          as.character(start_date) <= ymd &
          as.character(end_date)   >= ymd,
        unique(as.character(service_id))
      ]
      active <- union(active, base_active)
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(cdat) && nrow(cdat) > 0) {
    cdat <- as.data.table(cdat)
    added   <- cdat[as.character(date) == ymd & exception_type == 1,
                    unique(as.character(service_id))]
    removed <- cdat[as.character(date) == ymd & exception_type == 2,
                    unique(as.character(service_id))]
    active  <- setdiff(union(active, added), removed)
  }
  unique(active)
}

time_to_sec <- function(hms) {
  # Handles GTFS times > 24:00:00 (i.e., after midnight on the service day)
  parts <- strsplit(as.character(hms), ":", fixed = TRUE)
  vapply(parts, function(p) {
    if (length(p) < 3 || any(is.na(p))) return(NA_real_)
    as.numeric(p[1]) * 3600 + as.numeric(p[2]) * 60 + as.numeric(p[3])
  }, numeric(1))
}
```

### Load GTFS feeds

Multiple feeds supported — Sound Transit (`40_gtfs.zip`) for Link 1/2 Line,
Seattle Center Monorail (`96_gtfs.zip`) for the Monorail.

```{r discover-feeds}
gtfs_zips <- vapply(
  params$link_gtfs_paths,
  function(p) normalizePath(p, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE),
  character(1)
)
data.frame(feed = basename(gtfs_zips), path = gtfs_zips)
```

### Identify rail routes by route_id

We filter by `route_id` (not `route_short_name`) so the three lines resolve
unambiguously across feeds, regardless of how each agency labels them.

```{r identify-rail-routes}
target_ids <- as.character(params$link_route_ids)

rail_routes <- bind_rows(lapply(gtfs_zips, function(z) {
  routes <- read_gtfs_member(z, "routes.txt")
  if (is.null(routes)) return(NULL)
  routes <- as.data.table(routes)
  routes[, route_id := as.character(route_id)]
  matched <- routes[route_id %in% target_ids]
  if (nrow(matched) == 0L) return(NULL)
  matched[, feed := basename(z)]
  out_cols <- intersect(
    c("feed", "route_id", "route_short_name", "route_long_name",
      "route_type", "route_color"),
    names(matched)
  )
  matched[, ..out_cols]
}))

missing <- setdiff(target_ids, rail_routes$route_id)
if (length(missing) > 0L) {
  stop("Requested route_ids not found in any feed: ",
       paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}

rail_routes
```

### Process a single rail route

For one `route_id`, do everything: pull active trips on the service date,
get stops with lat/lon, spatial-join to cells, compute midday interstation
travel times, build the Seattle-internal corridor sequence (the trip
visiting the most Seattle stops), and collapse runs of stations that
share the same 0.5 mi cell.

```{r process-rail-route-fn}
process_rail_route <- function(route_id, zipfile, service_date,
                               grid_cells, planar_crs,
                               tt_window_start, tt_window_end) {
  rid <- as.character(route_id)

  routes <- read_gtfs_member(zipfile, "routes.txt")     %>% as.data.table()
  trips  <- read_gtfs_member(zipfile, "trips.txt")      %>% as.data.table()
  stops  <- read_gtfs_member(zipfile, "stops.txt")      %>% as.data.table()
  st     <- read_gtfs_member(zipfile, "stop_times.txt") %>% as.data.table()

  routes[, route_id := as.character(route_id)]
  trips [, route_id := as.character(route_id)]
  trips [, trip_id  := as.character(trip_id)]
  st    [, trip_id  := as.character(trip_id)]
  st    [, stop_id  := as.character(stop_id)]
  stops [, stop_id  := as.character(stop_id)]

  route_info <- routes[route_id == rid]
  stopifnot(nrow(route_info) >= 1L)

  svc_ids     <- active_service_ids(zipfile, service_date)
  route_trips <- trips[route_id == rid & as.character(service_id) %in% svc_ids]
  if (nrow(route_trips) == 0L) {
    warning("No active trips for route_id ", rid, " on ", service_date)
    return(NULL)
  }
  route_st <- st[trip_id %in% route_trips$trip_id]

  # Unique stops with one row per stop_id (parent stations + platforms can duplicate)
  route_stops_unique <- stops[stop_id %in% unique(route_st$stop_id),
    .(stop_name = first(na.omit(stop_name)),
      stop_lat  = mean(as.numeric(stop_lat), na.rm = TRUE),
      stop_lon  = mean(as.numeric(stop_lon), na.rm = TRUE)),
    by = stop_id
  ][!is.na(stop_lat) & !is.na(stop_lon)]

  stops_sf <- st_as_sf(
    route_stops_unique,
    coords = c("stop_lon", "stop_lat"),
    crs    = 4326
  ) %>% st_transform(planar_crs)

  stops_sf <- stops_sf %>%
    st_join(grid_cells %>% select(cell_id), join = st_intersects) %>%
    mutate(in_seattle_grid = !is.na(cell_id))

  # Midday interstation segment times (averaged across trips in the window)
  route_st[, arr_sec := time_to_sec(arrival_time)]
  route_st[, dep_sec := time_to_sec(departure_time)]
  trip_start <- route_st[, .(start_sec = min(dep_sec, na.rm = TRUE)),
                          by = trip_id]
  mid_lo <- time_to_sec(tt_window_start)
  mid_hi <- time_to_sec(tt_window_end)
  midday_trips <- trip_start[start_sec >= mid_lo & start_sec <= mid_hi, trip_id]
  if (length(midday_trips) == 0L) midday_trips <- unique(route_st$trip_id)

  mid_st <- route_st[trip_id %in% midday_trips]
  setorder(mid_st, trip_id, stop_sequence)
  mid_st[, next_stop_id := shift(stop_id, type = "lead"), by = trip_id]
  mid_st[, next_arr_sec := shift(arr_sec, type = "lead"), by = trip_id]
  mid_st[, dt_sec       := next_arr_sec - dep_sec]

  seg_times <- mid_st[!is.na(next_stop_id) & !is.na(dt_sec) & dt_sec > 0,
                      .(seg_sec_mean   = mean(dt_sec),
                        seg_sec_median = median(dt_sec),
                        n_trips        = .N),
                      by = .(from_stop = stop_id, to_stop = next_stop_id)]

  # Canonical Seattle-internal sequence: pick the trip visiting the most
  # Seattle-grid stops, use its stop_sequence ordering.
  seattle_stop_ids <- stops_sf %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(in_seattle_grid) %>% pull(stop_id)
  if (length(seattle_stop_ids) == 0L) {
    warning("Route ", rid, " has no stops in the Seattle grid.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  trip_cov <- mid_st[stop_id %in% seattle_stop_ids,
                     .(n = uniqueN(stop_id)),
                     by = trip_id][order(-n)]
  canonical_trip <- trip_cov$trip_id[1]

  canonical_seq <- mid_st[
    trip_id == canonical_trip & stop_id %in% seattle_stop_ids,
    .(stop_id, stop_sequence, arr_sec, dep_sec)
  ][order(stop_sequence)] %>%
    left_join(
      stops_sf %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
        filter(in_seattle_grid) %>%
        select(stop_id, stop_name, cell_id),
      by = "stop_id"
    )

  # Collapse runs of same-cell consecutive stations into single corridor entries
  corridor_cells <- canonical_seq %>%
    filter(!is.na(cell_id)) %>%
    mutate(run_id = cumsum(cell_id != lag(cell_id, default = -1L))) %>%
    group_by(run_id) %>%
    summarize(
      cell_id     = first(cell_id),
      stop_ids    = paste(stop_id, collapse = "|"),
      stop_names  = paste(unique(stop_name), collapse = " / "),
      arr_sec_in  = first(arr_sec),
      dep_sec_out = last(dep_sec),
      .groups     = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(run_id) %>%
    mutate(
      corridor_pos   = row_number(),
      next_cell_id   = lead(cell_id),
      dt_to_next_sec = lead(arr_sec_in) - dep_sec_out
    )

  list(
    route_id          = rid,
    route_short_name  = as.character(route_info$route_short_name[1]),
    route_long_name   = if ("route_long_name" %in% names(route_info))
                          as.character(route_info$route_long_name[1])
                        else NA_character_,
    route_color_hex   = if ("route_color" %in% names(route_info) &&
                            !is.na(route_info$route_color[1]) &&
                            nzchar(route_info$route_color[1]))
                          paste0("#", as.character(route_info$route_color[1]))
                        else NA_character_,
    feed              = basename(zipfile),
    stops_sf          = stops_sf,
    seg_times         = seg_times,
    corridor_cells    = corridor_cells
  )
}
```

### Build the list of rail corridors

We need the grid + p-median outputs in scope for the spatial join and
overlap flagging — load once, share across all rail routes.

```{r build-rail-corridors}
grid_demand <- readRDS(params$grid_demand_rds)
pmed        <- readRDS(params$pmedian_rds)
node_cell_ids <- pmed$nodes$cell_id

rail_corridors <- lapply(target_ids, function(rid) {
  feed_basename <- rail_routes[route_id == rid, feed][1]
  zipfile       <- gtfs_zips[basename(gtfs_zips) == feed_basename][1]
  process_rail_route(
    route_id        = rid,
    zipfile         = zipfile,
    service_date    = params$service_date,
    grid_cells      = grid_demand,
    planar_crs      = params$planar_crs,
    tt_window_start = params$tt_window_start,
    tt_window_end   = params$tt_window_end
  )
})
names(rail_corridors) <- target_ids
rail_corridors <- rail_corridors[!vapply(rail_corridors, is.null, logical(1))]

# Inspect per-route
for (rc in rail_corridors) {
  n_sea <- nrow(rc$stops_sf %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% filter(in_seattle_grid))
  cat(sprintf("\n--- %s (route_id=%s, feed=%s) — %d Seattle stations in %d cells ---\n",
              rc$route_short_name, rc$route_id, rc$feed,
              n_sea, nrow(rc$corridor_cells)))
  print(rc$corridor_cells %>%
          select(corridor_pos, cell_id, stop_names, dt_to_next_sec))
}
```

### Flag p-median overlap per rail line

```{r rail-pmedian-overlap}
for (i in seq_along(rail_corridors)) {
  rail_corridors[[i]]$corridor_cells <- rail_corridors[[i]]$corridor_cells %>%
    mutate(is_pmedian_node = cell_id %in% node_cell_ids)
}

overlap_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(rail_corridors, function(rc) {
  rc$corridor_cells %>%
    filter(is_pmedian_node) %>%
    transmute(route_short_name = rc$route_short_name,
              route_id         = rc$route_id,
              cell_id, corridor_pos, stop_names)
}))
overlap_summary
```

### Save the rail corridors

```{r save-rail-corridors}
saveRDS(
  list(
    corridors    = rail_corridors,
    service_date = as.character(params$service_date),
    tt_window    = c(params$tt_window_start, params$tt_window_end),
    source_feeds = basename(gtfs_zips)
  ),
  file.path(params$out_dir, "rail_corridors.rds")
)

# Flat CSV across all corridors for easy inspection
fwrite(
  bind_rows(lapply(rail_corridors, function(rc) {
    rc$corridor_cells %>%
      mutate(route_id = rc$route_id,
             route_short_name = rc$route_short_name)
  })) %>%
    select(route_id, route_short_name, corridor_pos, cell_id,
           stop_names, dt_to_next_sec, is_pmedian_node),
  file.path(params$out_dir, "rail_corridor_cells.csv")
)

# Per-line interstation times (concatenated)
fwrite(
  bind_rows(lapply(rail_corridors, function(rc) {
    rc$seg_times %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      mutate(route_id = rc$route_id,
             route_short_name = rc$route_short_name) %>%
      select(route_id, route_short_name, everything())
  })),
  file.path(params$out_dir, "rail_interstation_times.csv")
)
```

## Node-pair demand matrix

For each pair of p-median nodes (i, j), compute total trip demand whose
origin is in i's Voronoi cell and destination is in j's Voronoi cell.
This is the "natural market" for direct service between the two nodes.

### Build parcel → node lookup

Each parcel is in a cell; each cell is already assigned to a p-median node
(the `assigned_node` column from step 1). Chain them.

```{r parcel-to-node}
parcel_dt <- fread(params$parcel_map_csv)
parcel_dt[, ParcelID := as.character(ParcelID)]

parcel_sf <- st_as_sf(parcel_dt, wkt = "geometry", crs = params$planar_crs) %>%
  filter(CityName == "Seattle")

parcel_cell_map <- parcel_sf %>%
  st_join(grid_demand %>% select(cell_id), join = st_intersects) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(ParcelID, cell_id) %>%
  filter(!is.na(cell_id)) %>%
  distinct(ParcelID, .keep_all = TRUE)

# `grid_demand_*.rds` was saved before the p-median enrichment, so the
# cell→node assignment is in `pmed$assignment`, not `grid_demand`.
cell_node_lookup <- pmed$assignment %>%
  select(cell_id, assigned_node)

parcel_node <- parcel_cell_map %>%
  inner_join(cell_node_lookup, by = "cell_id") %>%
  select(ParcelID, node_cell = assigned_node)

cat(sprintf("Parcels mapped to nodes: %d\n", nrow(parcel_node)))
```

### DuckDB query: trips grouped by (origin_node, dest_node)

```{r node-pair-demand}
con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = ":memory:")
dbExecute(con, "PRAGMA threads=12;")
dbWriteTable(con, "parcel_node", parcel_node, overwrite = TRUE)
dbExecute(con, "CREATE INDEX idx_pn ON parcel_node(ParcelID);")

trips_rel <- sprintf(
  "read_csv_auto('%s', delim='\\t', header=true, quote='\"', escape='\"')",
  normalizePath(params$trips_tsv, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
)

sql <- sprintf("
  SELECT pn_o.node_cell AS origin_node,
         pn_d.node_cell AS dest_node,
         SUM(COALESCE(CAST(t.trexpfac AS DOUBLE), 0.0)) AS demand
  FROM %s t
  JOIN parcel_node pn_o ON CAST(t.opcl AS VARCHAR) = pn_o.ParcelID
  JOIN parcel_node pn_d ON CAST(t.dpcl AS VARCHAR) = pn_d.ParcelID
  GROUP BY 1, 2
", trips_rel)

node_pair_demand <- dbGetQuery(con, sql) %>%
  mutate(origin_node = as.integer(origin_node),
         dest_node   = as.integer(dest_node))
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("Node-pair demand rows: %d\n", nrow(node_pair_demand)))
cat(sprintf("Total intra-Seattle demand (both ends in some node's catchment): %s\n",
            format(round(sum(node_pair_demand$demand)), big.mark = ",")))
```

### Pivot to a demand matrix

```{r demand-matrix}
node_ids <- sort(pmed$nodes$cell_id)
n_nodes  <- length(node_ids)

W_directed <- matrix(0, n_nodes, n_nodes,
                     dimnames = list(node_ids, node_ids))
for (k in seq_len(nrow(node_pair_demand))) {
  i <- match(node_pair_demand$origin_node[k], node_ids)
  j <- match(node_pair_demand$dest_node[k],   node_ids)
  if (!is.na(i) && !is.na(j)) {
    W_directed[i, j] <- node_pair_demand$demand[k]
  }
}

# Symmetric undirected demand — corridor design treats lines as bidirectional
W <- W_directed + t(W_directed)
diag(W) <- 0   # self-trips don't motivate a corridor

# Sanity: top 10 node pairs by undirected demand
top_pairs <- as.data.frame(as.table(W)) %>%
  rename(node_a = Var1, node_b = Var2, demand = Freq) %>%
  filter(as.integer(as.character(node_a)) < as.integer(as.character(node_b))) %>%
  arrange(desc(demand)) %>%
  head(10)
top_pairs
```

## Dodgr setup: road graph + node-to-vertex matching

We use the cached PSRC motorcar graph (built by `StreetSetup.Rmd`).
Each p-median node centroid gets snapped to its nearest connected graph vertex.

```{r dodgr-load}
if (!file.exists(params$graph_rds)) stop("No dodgr graph available. Run StreetSetup.Rmd first.")
graph <- readRDS(params$graph_rds)
cat(sprintf("Loaded dodgr graph: %d edges\n", nrow(graph)))

# Drop `service` highways (alleys, parking-lot access, driveways).
# Convention from Phase2RunSimulation.Rmd: service edges add routing
# noise and rarely serve through-traffic. They've caused real perf and
# correctness problems on this project before.
if ("highway" %in% colnames(graph)) {
  n_before <- nrow(graph)
  graph    <- graph[as.character(graph$highway) != "service", , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("Dropped service edges: %d → %d (%d removed)\n",
              n_before, nrow(graph), n_before - nrow(graph)))
} else {
  warning("Graph has no `highway` column — service filter skipped. ",
          "Routes may include alleys/driveways.")
}

# Re-extract the largest connected component — removing service edges can
# orphan pieces that were only reachable through them.
n_before <- nrow(graph)
graph    <- dodgr::dodgr_components(graph)
graph    <- graph[graph$component == 1L, , drop = FALSE]
cat(sprintf("Largest component: %d → %d edges (%d dropped in smaller components)\n",
            n_before, nrow(graph), n_before - nrow(graph)))

cat(sprintf("Final graph: %d edges, %d distinct way_ids\n",
            nrow(graph), length(unique(graph$way_id))))
```

```{r node-to-vertex}
# Default node anchor = cell centroid. We may override per-cell below using
# the ArcGIS-snapped shapefile.
nodes_sf <- grid_demand %>%
  filter(cell_id %in% node_ids) %>%
  arrange(match(cell_id, node_ids))

node_centroids_planar <- st_centroid(nodes_sf)
node_centroids_4326   <- st_transform(node_centroids_planar, 4326)
node_lonlat <- st_coordinates(node_centroids_4326)
colnames(node_lonlat) <- c("x", "y")  # dodgr expects x, y

# Override with snapped points if the shapefile is available.
# Guard each piece explicitly — nzchar(NULL) returns logical(0), which
# short-circuits weirdly, and file.exists(NULL) errors with
# "invalid 'file' argument". So check NULL / length / non-NA first.
snap_path <- params$snapped_stops_shp
has_snap  <- is.character(snap_path) &&
             length(snap_path) == 1L &&
             !is.na(snap_path) &&
             nzchar(snap_path) &&
             file.exists(snap_path)

snapped_cell_ids <- integer(0)

if (has_snap) {
  snap_sf <- sf::st_read(snap_path, quiet = TRUE)

  # Find the cell_id column (case-insensitive — ArcGIS sometimes uppercases)
  cid_col <- names(snap_sf)[grep("^cell_?id$", names(snap_sf), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
  if (is.na(cid_col)) {
    stop("Snapped shapefile is missing a `cell_id` column. Re-edit on top of ",
         "the exported `corridors_stops.shp`, which has it.")
  }

  # Re-project to 4326 if needed
  if (is.na(sf::st_crs(snap_sf)) || sf::st_crs(snap_sf)$epsg != 4326L) {
    snap_sf <- sf::st_transform(snap_sf, 4326)
  }
  snap_xy <- sf::st_coordinates(snap_sf)
  snap_lookup <- data.frame(
    cell_id = as.integer(snap_sf[[cid_col]]),
    x       = snap_xy[, "X"],
    y       = snap_xy[, "Y"],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  ord_in_lookup <- match(nodes_sf$cell_id, snap_lookup$cell_id)
  override_rows <- which(!is.na(ord_in_lookup))
  node_lonlat[override_rows, "x"] <- snap_lookup$x[ord_in_lookup[override_rows]]
  node_lonlat[override_rows, "y"] <- snap_lookup$y[ord_in_lookup[override_rows]]

  snapped_cell_ids <- nodes_sf$cell_id[override_rows]

  cat(sprintf("Node anchor source: snapped shapefile (%d / %d nodes overridden)\n",
              length(override_rows), nrow(nodes_sf)))

  missing_in_shp <- nodes_sf$cell_id[is.na(ord_in_lookup)]
  if (length(missing_in_shp) > 0) {
    warning("Snapped shapefile is missing these p-median cell_ids — ",
            "their nodes will use cell centroids: ",
            paste(missing_in_shp, collapse = ", "))
  }
} else {
  cat("Node anchor source: cell centroids (no snapped shapefile at: ",
      if (is.null(snap_path) || length(snap_path) == 0) "<unset>" else snap_path,
      ")\n", sep = "")
}

# Match each (overridden or centroid) anchor to its nearest CONNECTED graph vertex
graph_v   <- dodgr::dodgr_vertices(graph)
match_idx <- dodgr::match_pts_to_verts(graph_v,
                                       as.data.frame(node_lonlat),
                                       connected = TRUE)

node_info <- data.frame(
  node_idx      = seq_len(n_nodes),
  cell_id       = nodes_sf$cell_id,
  vertex_id     = graph_v$id[match_idx],
  lon           = node_lonlat[, "x"],
  lat           = node_lonlat[, "y"],
  anchor_source = ifelse(nodes_sf$cell_id %in% snapped_cell_ids,
                         "snapped", "centroid"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Buffered-access vertex sets — each node is a CATCHMENT, not a point.
# Routes can enter/exit via any graph vertex within `node_buffer_ft` of the
# canonical node lat/lon. node_vert_ids[[i]] is the vector of vertex IDs.
graph_v_planar <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(id = graph_v$id, x = graph_v$x, y = graph_v$y),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326
) %>% sf::st_transform(params$planar_crs)

buffer_ft_nodes <- params$node_buffer_ft
node_vert_ids   <- vector("list", n_nodes)
for (i in seq_len(n_nodes)) {
  if (buffer_ft_nodes <= 0) {
    node_vert_ids[[i]] <- node_info$vertex_id[i]   # single-vertex fallback
    next
  }
  pt <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(node_info$lon[i], node_info$lat[i])),
                   crs = 4326) %>% sf::st_transform(params$planar_crs)
  dists <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(graph_v_planar, pt))
  near <- which(dists <= buffer_ft_nodes)
  if (length(near) == 0L) {
    node_vert_ids[[i]] <- node_info$vertex_id[i]   # fallback: keep snapped
  } else {
    node_vert_ids[[i]] <- graph_v$id[near]
  }
}

cat(sprintf("Per-node candidate vertices (within %g ft): min=%g, median=%g, max=%g\n",
            buffer_ft_nodes,
            min(lengths(node_vert_ids)),
            median(lengths(node_vert_ids)),
            max(lengths(node_vert_ids))))

node_info
```

## Transfer points

Optional intersections / transit centers a bus can stop at while passing
by, to enable transfers between routes that don't share a p-median node.
A candidate corridor's road path is **not** re-routed to touch them — if
the natural path is within `transfer_buffer_ft` of one, the bus picks it
up. Transfer points carry zero demand themselves.

```{r load-transfer-points}
tp_path <- params$transfer_points_shp
has_tp  <- is.character(tp_path) &&
           length(tp_path) == 1L &&
           !is.na(tp_path) &&
           nzchar(tp_path) &&
           file.exists(tp_path)

if (has_tp) {
  transfer_pts_sf <- sf::st_read(tp_path, quiet = TRUE)

  # Find Name column (case-insensitive)
  name_col <- names(transfer_pts_sf)[
    grep("^name$", names(transfer_pts_sf), ignore.case = TRUE)
  ][1]
  if (is.na(name_col)) {
    transfer_pts_sf$Name <- sprintf("TP%02d", seq_len(nrow(transfer_pts_sf)))
    name_col <- "Name"
  }

  transfer_pts_4326   <- sf::st_transform(transfer_pts_sf, 4326)
  transfer_pts_planar <- sf::st_transform(transfer_pts_sf, params$planar_crs)

  tp_lonlat <- sf::st_coordinates(transfer_pts_4326)
  colnames(tp_lonlat) <- c("x", "y")

  tp_match <- dodgr::match_pts_to_verts(
    graph_v, as.data.frame(tp_lonlat), connected = TRUE
  )

  n_transfer <- nrow(transfer_pts_sf)

  transfer_info <- data.frame(
    tp_idx    = seq_len(n_transfer),
    name      = as.character(transfer_pts_sf[[name_col]]),
    vertex_id = graph_v$id[tp_match],
    lon       = tp_lonlat[, "x"],
    lat       = tp_lonlat[, "y"],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
} else {
  # No file — empty transfer set. Pipeline still works; just no extra hubs.
  transfer_pts_planar <- sf::st_sfc(crs = params$planar_crs)
  n_transfer    <- 0L
  transfer_info <- data.frame(
    tp_idx    = integer(0),
    name      = character(0),
    vertex_id = character(0),
    lon       = numeric(0),
    lat       = numeric(0),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

cat(sprintf("Transfer points loaded: %d\n", n_transfer))

# Buffered-access vertex sets for transfer points (same idea as nodes)
transfer_vert_ids <- vector("list", n_transfer)
if (n_transfer > 0L) {
  for (i in seq_len(n_transfer)) {
    if (buffer_ft_nodes <= 0) {
      transfer_vert_ids[[i]] <- transfer_info$vertex_id[i]
      next
    }
    pt <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(transfer_info$lon[i], transfer_info$lat[i])),
                     crs = 4326) %>% sf::st_transform(params$planar_crs)
    dists <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(graph_v_planar, pt))
    near <- which(dists <= buffer_ft_nodes)
    transfer_vert_ids[[i]] <- if (length(near) == 0L)
      transfer_info$vertex_id[i] else graph_v$id[near]
  }
  cat(sprintf("Per-TP candidate vertices: min=%g, median=%g, max=%g\n",
              min(lengths(transfer_vert_ids)),
              median(lengths(transfer_vert_ids)),
              max(lengths(transfer_vert_ids))))
}

transfer_info
```

## Enumerate candidate bus corridors

For each unordered pair (A, B) we generate one candidate corridor per
acceptable interior subset of other p-median nodes. A corridor
`A → C₁ → … → Cₖ → B` is **acceptable** if its total length on the road
graph is at most `max_detour_ratio` × direct(A, B). This lets the greedy
step combine pairs like `429 → 542 → 558` into a single line when
geographically reasonable, instead of picking three separate 2-node routes.

We also build the all-pairs road paths from dodgr (`all_paths`) — needed
later to draw each selected bus corridor's actual road geometry on the map.

```{r dodgr-all-paths}
# With buffered access we compute paths *between best access-vertex pairs*.
# For each (i, j), we pick the (vA ∈ node_vert_ids[[i]], vB ∈ node_vert_ids[[j]])
# pair that minimizes road travel time, then return the path between them.
# The node-distance-matrix chunk below computes the time matrix using the
# same buffered min, so the path geometry and the routing times are consistent.

v_idx_by_id <- setNames(seq_len(nrow(graph_v)), graph_v$id)

path_to_coords <- function(vertex_ids) {
  if (is.null(vertex_ids) || length(vertex_ids) < 2) return(NULL)
  idx <- v_idx_by_id[as.character(vertex_ids)]
  idx <- idx[!is.na(idx)]
  if (length(idx) < 2) return(NULL)
  cbind(graph_v$x[idx], graph_v$y[idx])
}
```

### All-stops time matrix

Time-based throughout — `dodgr_times()` uses the graph's per-edge travel
time (OSM `maxspeed` × edge length, weighted by the motorcar profile), so
freeway corridors get short times and local streets get long ones.
No more global `bus_speed_mph` constant.

The full matrix includes both p-median nodes and transfer points (if any),
so the same matrix supports the detour-ratio check (subset to p-median ×
p-median = `T_node_min`) and transfer-hub lookups.

```{r node-distance-matrix}
# Buffered routing: for each stop (node OR transfer point), we have multiple
# candidate access vertices. Travel time between two stops = min over all
# (vA, vB) candidate pairs of dodgr_times(vA, vB). Eliminates one-way-street
# artifacts that would otherwise inflate the time by forcing routes to
# loop around blocks to reach a single canonical vertex.

# All candidate vertices, with stop-index ownership (so we can sub-matrix)
stop_vert_ids <- c(node_vert_ids,
                   if (n_transfer > 0L) transfer_vert_ids else list())
all_vert_ids  <- unique(unlist(stop_vert_ids))
n_full        <- length(stop_vert_ids)

cat(sprintf("Routing over %d unique candidate vertices (%d stops total)\n",
            length(all_vert_ids), n_full))

# One big dodgr_times call — all candidates × all candidates
T_big_sec <- dodgr::dodgr_times(
  graph,
  from = all_vert_ids,
  to   = all_vert_ids
)

# For each (stop_i, stop_j), take the min travel time over candidate-vertex pairs.
T_full_min <- matrix(Inf, n_full, n_full)
for (i in seq_len(n_full)) {
  v_i_idx <- match(stop_vert_ids[[i]], all_vert_ids)
  for (j in seq_len(n_full)) {
    if (i == j) { T_full_min[i, j] <- 0; next }
    v_j_idx <- match(stop_vert_ids[[j]], all_vert_ids)
    sub <- T_big_sec[v_i_idx, v_j_idx, drop = FALSE]
    if (all(!is.finite(sub))) next
    T_full_min[i, j] <- min(sub, na.rm = TRUE) / 60
  }
}

T_node_min <- T_full_min[seq_len(n_nodes), seq_len(n_nodes), drop = FALSE]

dimnames(T_node_min) <- list(node_info$cell_id, node_info$cell_id)
dimnames(T_full_min) <- list(
  c(as.character(node_info$cell_id),
    if (n_transfer > 0) sprintf("TP_%s", transfer_info$name) else character(0)),
  c(as.character(node_info$cell_id),
    if (n_transfer > 0) sprintf("TP_%s", transfer_info$name) else character(0))
)

cat(sprintf("All-stops time matrix: %d × %d (p-median: %d, transfer: %d)\n",
            n_full, n_full, n_nodes, n_transfer))
cat(sprintf("P-median pairwise travel time: %.1f min — %.1f min (avg %.1f)\n",
            min(T_node_min[lower.tri(T_node_min)]),
            max(T_node_min[lower.tri(T_node_min)]),
            mean(T_node_min[lower.tri(T_node_min)])))

# Path geometry uses each node's PRIMARY snapped vertex (one per node), via the
# standard nested dodgr_paths call — reliable, positionally indexed as
# all_paths[[i]][[j]]. Routing TIMES above already use the buffered min, so the
# model isn't penalized by one-way access; only the *drawn* geometry uses a
# single canonical vertex (cosmetic).
all_paths <- dodgr::dodgr_paths(
  graph,
  from = node_info$vertex_id,
  to   = node_info$vertex_id,
  vertices = TRUE
)
```

### Detour-bounded enumeration

```{r enumerate-corridors}
# Enumeration runs on TIME (minutes) — detour ratio = corridor_time / direct_time.
enumerate_corridors_detour <- function(T_node, max_detour, max_nodes) {
  n <- nrow(T_node)
  out <- list()

  for (i in 1:(n - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):n) {
      direct <- T_node[i, j]
      if (!is.finite(direct) || direct == 0) next

      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- list(
        sequence        = c(i, j),
        path_length_min = direct,
        detour_ratio    = 1.0,
        pair_id         = sprintf("%d_%d", i, j)
      )

      others <- setdiff(seq_len(n), c(i, j))
      via    <- T_node[i, others] + T_node[others, j]
      ratios <- via / direct
      in_flight <- others[is.finite(ratios) & ratios <= max_detour]
      if (length(in_flight) == 0L) next

      for (cc in in_flight) {
        pl <- T_node[i, cc] + T_node[cc, j]
        out[[length(out) + 1]] <- list(
          sequence        = c(i, cc, j),
          path_length_min = pl,
          detour_ratio    = pl / direct,
          pair_id         = sprintf("%d_%d", i, j)
        )
      }

      max_interior <- min(length(in_flight), max_nodes - 2L)
      if (max_interior < 2L) next

      for (k in 2:max_interior) {
        subsets <- combn(in_flight, k, simplify = FALSE)
        for (subset in subsets) {
          ordered_subset <- subset[order(T_node[i, subset])]
          seq_v   <- c(i, ordered_subset, j)
          edges   <- cbind(seq_v[-length(seq_v)], seq_v[-1])
          pl      <- sum(T_node[edges])
          r       <- pl / direct
          if (r <= max_detour) {
            out[[length(out) + 1]] <- list(
              sequence        = seq_v,
              path_length_min = pl,
              detour_ratio    = r,
              pair_id         = sprintf("%d_%d", i, j)
            )
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  out
}

candidates <- enumerate_corridors_detour(
  T_node_min,
  max_detour = params$max_detour_ratio,
  max_nodes  = params$max_corridor_nodes
)

cat(sprintf("Enumerated %d candidate corridors (max_detour = %.2f, max_nodes = %d)\n",
            length(candidates), params$max_detour_ratio, params$max_corridor_nodes))

table(corridor_length_in_nodes =
        vapply(candidates, function(c) length(c$sequence), integer(1)))
```

### Augment candidates with transfer points

For each ordered p-median pair `(i, j)`, find transfer points whose
location is within `transfer_buffer_ft` of the dodgr road path `i → j`,
ordered by their projected position along the path. Then walk each
candidate corridor and insert those transfer points between consecutive
p-median nodes — the corridor's road geometry is unchanged; we just pick
up extra stops.

```{r augment-candidates}
# Distance of a point's perpendicular projection along a linestring,
# in the line's CRS units. Used to ORDER transfer points along a path.
project_distance_along_line <- function(line_sf, point_sf) {
  lc <- sf::st_coordinates(line_sf)
  pc <- sf::st_coordinates(point_sf)
  px <- pc[1, "X"]; py <- pc[1, "Y"]
  n  <- nrow(lc)
  if (n < 2) return(NA_real_)
  best_d2 <- Inf; best_pos <- 0; cum_dist <- 0
  for (k in seq_len(n - 1)) {
    x1 <- lc[k,     "X"]; y1 <- lc[k,     "Y"]
    x2 <- lc[k + 1L,"X"]; y2 <- lc[k + 1L,"Y"]
    dx <- x2 - x1; dy <- y2 - y1
    seg_len2 <- dx * dx + dy * dy
    if (seg_len2 == 0) next
    seg_len <- sqrt(seg_len2)
    t <- ((px - x1) * dx + (py - y1) * dy) / seg_len2
    t <- max(0, min(1, t))
    proj_x <- x1 + t * dx; proj_y <- y1 + t * dy
    d2     <- (px - proj_x)^2 + (py - proj_y)^2
    if (d2 < best_d2) {
      best_d2  <- d2
      best_pos <- cum_dist + t * seg_len
    }
    cum_dist <- cum_dist + seg_len
  }
  best_pos
}

buffer_ft <- params$transfer_buffer_ft
dwell_min <- params$express_dwell_sec / 60

# Precompute near_T[[i, j]] = ordered transfer-point indices on dodgr path i→j
near_T <- vector("list", n_nodes * n_nodes)
dim(near_T) <- c(n_nodes, n_nodes)

if (n_transfer > 0L) {
  for (i in seq_len(n_nodes)) {
    for (j in seq_len(n_nodes)) {
      if (i == j) { near_T[[i, j]] <- integer(0); next }
      vids   <- all_paths[[i]][[j]]
      coords <- path_to_coords(vids)
      if (is.null(coords) || nrow(coords) < 2) {
        near_T[[i, j]] <- integer(0); next
      }
      line_planar <- sf::st_linestring(coords) |>
        sf::st_sfc(crs = 4326) |>
        sf::st_transform(params$planar_crs)
      dists <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(transfer_pts_planar, line_planar))
      near_idx <- which(dists <= buffer_ft)
      if (length(near_idx) == 0L) {
        near_T[[i, j]] <- integer(0); next
      }
      positions <- vapply(near_idx, function(k) {
        pt <- sf::st_geometry(transfer_pts_planar)[k]
        project_distance_along_line(line_planar, pt)
      }, numeric(1))
      near_T[[i, j]] <- near_idx[order(positions)]
    }
  }
} else {
  # No transfer points → all empty
  for (i in seq_len(n_nodes)) for (j in seq_len(n_nodes)) {
    near_T[[i, j]] <- integer(0)
  }
}

# Augment one corridor's p-median sequence with transfer-point indices
# (offset by n_nodes) and compute cumulative arrival times along the
# resulting full stop sequence. Each non-initial stop adds `dwell_min`
# at the previous stop plus the segment time to itself.
augment_corridor <- function(seq_v, near_T, T_full_min, dwell_min, n_nodes) {
  full <- integer(0)
  for (k in seq_along(seq_v)) {
    full <- c(full, seq_v[k])
    if (k < length(seq_v)) {
      tps <- near_T[[seq_v[k], seq_v[k + 1]]]
      if (length(tps) > 0L) full <- c(full, n_nodes + tps)
    }
  }
  if (length(full) < 2L) {
    cum_t <- 0
  } else {
    edges <- cbind(full[-length(full)], full[-1])
    seg_t <- T_full_min[edges]
    cum_t <- c(0, cumsum(seg_t + dwell_min))
  }
  list(full_seq = full, cum_t = cum_t)
}

for (i in seq_along(candidates)) {
  aug <- augment_corridor(candidates[[i]]$sequence, near_T, T_full_min,
                          dwell_min, n_nodes)
  candidates[[i]]$full_seq         <- aug$full_seq
  candidates[[i]]$cum_t            <- aug$cum_t
  candidates[[i]]$n_transfer_stops <- length(aug$full_seq) -
                                      length(candidates[[i]]$sequence)
  candidates[[i]]$travel_time_min  <- if (length(aug$cum_t) > 0L)
                                        tail(aug$cum_t, 1) else 0
}

n_with_tp <- sum(vapply(candidates,
                        function(c) c$n_transfer_stops > 0L, logical(1)))
cat(sprintf("Augmented %d candidates with transfer points (buffer = %d ft); %d pick up ≥1 TP\n",
            length(candidates), buffer_ft, n_with_tp))
```

## Greedy with quality-threshold stopping

For each unordered node-pair (i, j) we compute the **service quality**:

> `quality(i, j) = T_service(i, j) / T_direct_road(i, j)`

where `T_service` is the fastest of:
- riding a single selected corridor from i to j (along the corridor's actual
  stop-by-stop path, which may detour through intermediates),
- transferring at some hub h (best corridor i→h + 2.5 min + best corridor h→j).

A pair is **served** if `quality ≤ 1 + quality_threshold_pct` (e.g., ≤1.5×
direct road time when threshold = 0.5). Pairs that exceed this threshold —
or are flat-out unreachable — incur a **penalty** = demand × excess time
above threshold. Unreachable pairs are assigned `quality = unreachable_quality`
so the penalty is large but finite.

**Greedy stops when total penalty hits zero** (every pair meets the
quality threshold), not when a corridor budget is hit. Since penalty is
weighted by demand, the heuristic naturally drives high-volume pairs to
quality ≈ 1 first; low-volume pairs end up at quality closer to the
threshold (or, if the safety cap is hit, slightly above).

```{r greedy-with-transfer}
cell_to_node_idx <- setNames(node_info$node_idx, as.character(node_info$cell_id))

# Rail cell sequences → p-median node indices
rail_node_seqs <- lapply(rail_corridors, function(rc) {
  seq_v <- rc$corridor_cells %>%
    filter(is_pmedian_node) %>%
    arrange(corridor_pos) %>%
    pull(cell_id) %>%
    as.character() %>%
    cell_to_node_idx[.] %>%
    unname()
  seq_v[!is.na(seq_v)]
})

for (i in seq_along(rail_node_seqs)) {
  rc    <- rail_corridors[[i]]
  seq_v <- rail_node_seqs[[i]]
  cat(sprintf("%-15s covers %d p-median nodes: %s\n",
              rc$route_short_name, length(seq_v),
              if (length(seq_v) > 0)
                paste(node_info$cell_id[seq_v], collapse = ", ")
              else "(none)"))
}

transfer_pen        <- params$transfer_penalty_min
quality_threshold   <- 1 + params$quality_threshold_pct
unreachable_quality <- params$unreachable_quality

# For a set of selected corridors, compute the best service time for every
# node-pair. Each corridor carries `full_seq` (p-median + transfer stops)
# and `cum_t` (cumulative arrival times along that sequence, including
# stop dwell), both built at enumeration time. Travel time between any
# two stops on a corridor = abs(cum_t[b] - cum_t[a]).
#
# Transfer points (indices > n_nodes) carry zero demand but ARE valid hubs
# — so a pair (i, j) of p-median nodes can be served via a transfer point
# h shared between two different corridors.
compute_service <- function(selected, transfer_pen, n_full, n_nodes) {
  T_direct <- matrix(Inf, n_full, n_full)
  diag(T_direct) <- 0

  for (c in selected) {
    full_seq <- c$full_seq
    cum_t    <- c$cum_t
    if (is.null(full_seq) || length(full_seq) < 2L) next

    K <- length(full_seq)
    for (a in 1:K) {
      ti <- full_seq[a]
      for (b in 1:K) {
        if (a == b) next
        tj <- full_seq[b]
        t_ab <- abs(cum_t[b] - cum_t[a])
        if (t_ab < T_direct[ti, tj]) T_direct[ti, tj] <- t_ab
      }
    }
  }

  # Hub iteration includes transfer points (indices > n_nodes)
  T_service <- T_direct[seq_len(n_nodes), seq_len(n_nodes), drop = FALSE]
  for (i in 1:(n_nodes - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):n_nodes) {
      for (h in seq_len(n_full)) {
        if (h == i || h == j) next
        if (is.finite(T_direct[i, h]) && is.finite(T_direct[h, j])) {
          via_h <- T_direct[i, h] + transfer_pen + T_direct[h, j]
          if (via_h < T_service[i, j]) {
            T_service[i, j] <- via_h
            T_service[j, i] <- via_h
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }

  list(
    direct  = T_direct[seq_len(n_nodes), seq_len(n_nodes), drop = FALSE],
    service = T_service
  )
}

# Penalty: demand-weighted travel-time excess above the quality threshold.
# Unreachable pairs are treated as if quality = unreachable_quality.
compute_penalty <- function(T_service, W, T_road, quality_threshold,
                            unreachable_quality) {
  n <- nrow(W)
  effective <- T_service
  unreach <- !is.finite(effective)
  effective[unreach] <- T_road[unreach] * unreachable_quality

  threshold_time <- quality_threshold * T_road
  excess  <- pmax(0, effective - threshold_time)
  penalty <- W * excess
  diag(penalty) <- 0

  quality <- effective / pmax(T_road, 1e-9)

  list(
    total       = sum(penalty[lower.tri(penalty)]),
    per_pair    = penalty,
    quality     = quality,
    n_over      = sum(excess[lower.tri(excess)] > 0),
    n_unreach   = sum(unreach[lower.tri(unreach)])
  )
}

# Initialize: rail pre-seed. Rail corridors don't auto-pick-up transfer
# points (their geometry isn't a dodgr road path), so full_seq = sequence,
# and cum_t uses T_node_min for consecutive p-median pairs + dwell at each
# stop.
selected_corridors <- list()
prev_penalty <- Inf
for (i in seq_along(rail_corridors)) {
  rc    <- rail_corridors[[i]]
  seq_v <- rail_node_seqs[[i]]

  if (length(seq_v) >= 2L) {
    edges_r <- cbind(seq_v[-length(seq_v)], seq_v[-1])
    seg_t_r <- T_node_min[edges_r]
    cum_t_r <- c(0, cumsum(seg_t_r + dwell_min))
  } else {
    cum_t_r <- 0
  }

  selected_corridors[[length(selected_corridors) + 1]] <- list(
    type            = "rail",
    label           = rc$route_short_name,
    sequence        = seq_v,
    full_seq        = seq_v,
    cum_t           = cum_t_r,
    path_length_min = if (length(cum_t_r) > 0L) tail(cum_t_r, 1) else NA_real_,
    detour_ratio    = NA_real_,
    marginal_demand = NA_real_
  )
  st  <- compute_service(selected_corridors, transfer_pen, n_full, n_nodes)
  pen <- compute_penalty(st$service, W, T_node_min, quality_threshold,
                         unreachable_quality)
  if (!is.finite(prev_penalty)) {
    base_pen <- compute_penalty(
      matrix(Inf, n_nodes, n_nodes),
      W, T_node_min, quality_threshold, unreachable_quality
    )$total
    prev_penalty <- base_pen
  }
  selected_corridors[[length(selected_corridors)]]$marginal_demand <-
    prev_penalty - pen$total
  prev_penalty <- pen$total
}

cat(sprintf("\nAfter rail pre-seed: penalty = %s, %d pairs over threshold, %d unreachable\n",
            format(round(prev_penalty), big.mark = ","),
            pen$n_over, pen$n_unreach))

# Greedy: keep adding bus corridors until total penalty hits zero
remaining     <- candidates
n_total_pairs <- n_nodes * (n_nodes - 1) / 2
max_step      <- params$n_bus_corridors
step          <- 0

while (TRUE) {
  if (prev_penalty == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("\n*** All %d pairs meet quality threshold (≤%.0f%% slower than direct) after %d bus corridor(s). ***\n",
                n_total_pairs, params$quality_threshold_pct * 100, step))
    break
  }
  if (step >= max_step) {
    message("Hit safety cap of ", max_step, " bus corridors. ",
            pen$n_over, " pairs still over threshold (", pen$n_unreach,
            " unreachable). Stopping.")
    break
  }
  if (length(remaining) == 0L) {
    message("Candidate set exhausted. ", pen$n_over, " pairs still over threshold.")
    break
  }

  scores <- vapply(remaining, function(c) {
    test <- c(selected_corridors, list(c))
    st_new  <- compute_service(test, transfer_pen, n_full, n_nodes)
    pen_new <- compute_penalty(st_new$service, W, T_node_min,
                               quality_threshold, unreachable_quality)
    prev_penalty - pen_new$total
  }, numeric(1))

  if (max(scores) <= 0) {
    message("No remaining candidate reduces penalty. ",
            pen$n_over, " pairs still over threshold. Stopping.")
    break
  }

  step <- step + 1L
  best_idx <- which.max(scores)
  best     <- remaining[[best_idx]]
  best$type            <- "bus"
  best$label           <- sprintf("Bus %d", step)
  best$marginal_demand <- scores[best_idx]

  selected_corridors[[length(selected_corridors) + 1]] <- best
  remaining <- remaining[-best_idx]

  st  <- compute_service(selected_corridors, transfer_pen, n_full, n_nodes)
  pen <- compute_penalty(st$service, W, T_node_min, quality_threshold,
                         unreachable_quality)
  prev_penalty <- pen$total

  cat(sprintf("[%2d] %s: %d nodes (+%d TP), %.1f min (det %.2f), Δpenalty = %s, total = %s (over %d, unreach %d)\n",
              step, best$label,
              length(best$sequence),
              best$n_transfer_stops %||% 0L,
              best$travel_time_min %||% best$path_length_min %||% NA,
              best$detour_ratio,
              format(round(best$marginal_demand), big.mark = ","),
              format(round(prev_penalty), big.mark = ","),
              pen$n_over, pen$n_unreach))
}

# Hold the final state for downstream chunks
state <- list(
  service        = st$service,
  direct         = st$direct,
  penalty_total  = pen$total,
  quality        = pen$quality,
  per_pair       = pen$per_pair,
  n_over         = pen$n_over,
  n_unreach      = pen$n_unreach
)

# Final quality stats

cat(sprintf("\n=== Final coverage ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Pairs at or below %.0f%% threshold: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            params$quality_threshold_pct * 100,
            n_total_pairs - pen$n_over, n_total_pairs,
            100 * (n_total_pairs - pen$n_over) / n_total_pairs))
cat(sprintf("Pairs unreachable (≥2 transfers needed): %d\n", pen$n_unreach))
cat(sprintf("Avg quality across all pairs: %.2f\n",
            mean(pen$quality[lower.tri(pen$quality)])))
cat(sprintf("Demand-weighted avg quality: %.2f\n",
            sum(pen$quality[lower.tri(pen$quality)] *
                W[lower.tri(W)]) / sum(W[lower.tri(W)])))
```

## ILP-based corridor selection (overrides greedy)

Reformulates the corridor selection as a Mixed Integer Linear Program with
explicit pair-coverage + rightsizing constraints. Globally optimal subject
to the formulation (greedy is locally optimal).

**Decision variables:** `x_c ∈ {0,1}` for each candidate bus corridor.

**Auxiliary variables:**
- `u[t] ∈ {0,1}` — one per *viable transfer triple* `(i, j, h)`. A triple is
  viable only if the best-case via-`h` time (`T(i,h) + penalty + T(h,j)`) is
  within the pair's quality budget `qt × T(i,j)` — i.e., the hub is genuinely
  on-path. The leftover slack is split evenly between the two legs, and `u[t]`
  can fire only if a selected corridor (or rail) serves each leg within its
  share. So a transfer-covered pair is **guaranteed** at quality ≤ qt — no more
  off-path hubs faking coverage.
- `slack[i, j] ∈ {0,1}` — fallback if a pair can't be covered (heavy
  demand-weighted penalty, so used only when otherwise infeasible).

**Constraints:**
1. *Pair coverage:* every node-pair served directly OR via a viable transfer
   OR slack, accounting for rail's pre-existing direct coverage.
2. *Rightsizing:* for each p-median node `i`,
   `Σ x_c × touches[c, i]  ≤  rightsize_tolerance × D_i × Σ x_c`.

**Objective:** minimize bus-corridor count + demand-weighted slack penalty.

Because the detour-bounded enumeration caps every candidate at ≤ 1.2 detour,
any pair *directly* served by a candidate is automatically quality ≤ 1.2, and
the viable-triple construction makes transfer coverage quality ≤ qt by design.
Rail corridors stay fixed; their direct + leg contributions enter as constants.

```{r ilp-corridor-selection}
required_pkgs <- c("ompr", "ompr.roi", "ROI", "ROI.plugin.highs", "highs")
missing_pkgs  <- required_pkgs[!vapply(required_pkgs,
                                       requireNamespace, logical(1),
                                       quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0L) {
  stop("Install: install.packages(c('",
       paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = "', '"), "'))")
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ompr)
  library(ompr.roi)
  library(ROI.plugin.highs)
})

N_cand    <- length(candidates)
tolerance <- params$rightsize_tolerance

# Demand share per p-median node (sums to 1)
D_share <- rowSums(W) / sum(W)

# Build candidate stop-pair time lookup from full_seq + cum_t
candidate_t <- vector("list", N_cand)
for (c_idx in seq_along(candidates)) {
  cc <- candidates[[c_idx]]
  fs <- cc$full_seq
  ct <- cc$cum_t
  if (is.null(fs) || length(fs) < 2L) {
    candidate_t[[c_idx]] <- NULL
    next
  }
  Mc <- matrix(Inf, n_full, n_full)
  K <- length(fs)
  for (a in 1:K) for (b in 1:K) {
    if (a == b) next
    Mc[fs[a], fs[b]] <- min(Mc[fs[a], fs[b]], abs(ct[b] - ct[a]))
  }
  candidate_t[[c_idx]] <- Mc
}

# direct_serves[c, i, j] = 1 if candidate c serves p-median pair (i,j) directly
# at quality ≤ threshold
direct_serves <- array(0L, dim = c(N_cand, n_nodes, n_nodes))
for (c_idx in 1:N_cand) {
  Mc <- candidate_t[[c_idx]]
  if (is.null(Mc)) next
  for (i in 1:n_nodes) for (j in 1:n_nodes) {
    if (i == j) next
    if (is.finite(Mc[i, j]) && Mc[i, j] <= quality_threshold * T_node_min[i, j]) {
      direct_serves[c_idx, i, j] <- 1L
    }
  }
}

# touches[c, i] = 1 if candidate c includes p-median node i in its sequence
touches <- matrix(0L, N_cand, n_nodes)
for (c_idx in 1:N_cand) {
  for (i in candidates[[c_idx]]$sequence) {
    touches[c_idx, i] <- 1L
  }
}

# Rail's pre-seed contribution. rail_direct[i,j] = 1 if a rail line serves pair
# (i,j) directly at quality ≤ threshold. rail_T[a,b] = best rail travel time
# between any two stops (used as a transfer-leg provider in viable triples below).
rail_direct <- matrix(0L, n_nodes, n_nodes)
rail_T      <- matrix(Inf, n_full, n_full)
for (sc in selected_corridors) {
  if (sc$type != "rail") next
  fs <- sc$full_seq; ct <- sc$cum_t
  if (is.null(fs) || length(fs) < 2L) next
  K <- length(fs)
  for (a in 1:K) for (b in 1:K) {
    if (a == b) next
    aa <- fs[a]; bb <- fs[b]
    t_ab <- abs(ct[b] - ct[a])
    rail_T[aa, bb] <- min(rail_T[aa, bb], t_ab)
    if (aa <= n_nodes && bb <= n_nodes && is.finite(t_ab) &&
        t_ab <= quality_threshold * T_node_min[aa, bb]) {
      rail_direct[aa, bb] <- 1L
    }
  }
}

cat(sprintf("ILP inputs ready: %d candidates, %d p-median nodes, %d total stops\n",
            N_cand, n_nodes, n_full))
cat(sprintf("Rail directly covers %d / %d pairs already\n",
            sum(rail_direct[lower.tri(rail_direct)]),
            n_nodes * (n_nodes - 1) / 2))

# ---- Dominance pre-filter ----
# Drop candidate B if some A directly serves every pair B serves AND touches a
# subset of B's nodes (≥ as good for coverage, ≤ as costly for equity), with at
# least one strict. Transfer-leg value is NOT part of dominance now (transfers
# are handled by viable triples below), so this stays conservative — it never
# drops a candidate that might uniquely provide a transfer leg.
cat("Running dominance pre-filter...\n")
t_pre <- Sys.time()

direct_sets  <- lapply(seq_len(N_cand), function(c) which(direct_serves[c, , ] == 1L))
touches_sets <- lapply(seq_len(N_cand), function(c) which(touches[c, ] == 1L))
is_subset <- function(a, b) length(a) == 0L || all(a %in% b)

keep <- rep(TRUE, N_cand)
for (b in seq_len(N_cand)) {
  if (!keep[b]) next
  for (a in seq_len(N_cand)) {
    if (a == b || !keep[a]) next
    if (length(direct_sets[[a]])  < length(direct_sets[[b]]))  next
    if (length(touches_sets[[a]]) > length(touches_sets[[b]])) next
    if (!is_subset(direct_sets[[b]],  direct_sets[[a]]))  next
    if (!is_subset(touches_sets[[a]], touches_sets[[b]])) next
    strict <- (length(direct_sets[[a]])  > length(direct_sets[[b]])) ||
              (length(touches_sets[[a]]) < length(touches_sets[[b]]))
    if (strict) { keep[b] <- FALSE; break }
  }
}

n_dropped <- N_cand - sum(keep)
cat(sprintf("  Pre-filter: %d → %d candidates (%d dominated, %.1fs)\n",
            N_cand, sum(keep), n_dropped,
            as.numeric(Sys.time() - t_pre, units = "secs")))

kept_idx      <- which(keep)
candidates    <- candidates[kept_idx]
candidate_t   <- candidate_t[kept_idx]
direct_serves <- direct_serves[kept_idx, , , drop = FALSE]
touches       <- touches[kept_idx, , drop = FALSE]
N_cand        <- length(candidates)

# ---- Viable transfer triples ----
# A transfer for pair (i,j) via hub h is viable only if the BEST-CASE total
# (direct legs + penalty) fits the pair quality budget:
#     T(i,h) + penalty + T(h,j)  ≤  qt × T(i,j)
# For each viable triple we split the leftover slack evenly between the two
# legs and record which candidates (and whether rail) serve each leg within
# its share. So if u[t] fires, the pair is genuinely served at quality ≤ qt.
qt  <- quality_threshold
pen <- transfer_pen
t_tri <- Sys.time()

triple_i <- integer(0); triple_j <- integer(0); triple_h <- integer(0)
triple_leg1 <- list(); triple_leg2 <- list()
triple_rail1 <- integer(0); triple_rail2 <- integer(0)

for (i in 1:(n_nodes - 1)) {
  for (j in (i + 1):n_nodes) {
    budget <- qt * T_node_min[i, j]
    for (h in 1:n_full) {
      if (h == i || h == j) next
      d_ih <- T_full_min[i, h]; d_hj <- T_full_min[h, j]
      best_via <- d_ih + pen + d_hj
      if (!is.finite(best_via) || best_via > budget) next   # non-viable hub
      slack_h <- budget - best_via
      L1 <- d_ih + slack_h / 2
      L2 <- d_hj + slack_h / 2
      leg1 <- which(vapply(candidate_t, function(Mc)
        !is.null(Mc) && is.finite(Mc[i, h]) && Mc[i, h] <= L1, logical(1)))
      leg2 <- which(vapply(candidate_t, function(Mc)
        !is.null(Mc) && is.finite(Mc[h, j]) && Mc[h, j] <= L2, logical(1)))
      r1 <- as.integer(is.finite(rail_T[i, h]) && rail_T[i, h] <= L1)
      r2 <- as.integer(is.finite(rail_T[h, j]) && rail_T[h, j] <= L2)
      if ((length(leg1) + r1 == 0L) || (length(leg2) + r2 == 0L)) next
      triple_i <- c(triple_i, i); triple_j <- c(triple_j, j); triple_h <- c(triple_h, h)
      triple_leg1[[length(triple_leg1) + 1]] <- leg1
      triple_leg2[[length(triple_leg2) + 1]] <- leg2
      triple_rail1 <- c(triple_rail1, r1); triple_rail2 <- c(triple_rail2, r2)
    }
  }
}
n_triples <- length(triple_i)
cat(sprintf("Viable transfer triples: %d (%.1fs)\n",
            n_triples, as.numeric(Sys.time() - t_tri, units = "secs")))

# Coefficient arrays for the model (dim ≥ 1 to avoid zero-length issues)
serves    <- array(0L, dim = c(max(1L, n_triples), n_nodes, n_nodes))
leg1_coef <- matrix(0L, max(1L, n_triples), N_cand)
leg2_coef <- matrix(0L, max(1L, n_triples), N_cand)
if (n_triples > 0L) {
  for (t in seq_len(n_triples)) {
    serves[t, triple_i[t], triple_j[t]] <- 1L
    if (length(triple_leg1[[t]]) > 0L) leg1_coef[t, triple_leg1[[t]]] <- 1L
    if (length(triple_leg2[[t]]) > 0L) leg2_coef[t, triple_leg2[[t]]] <- 1L
  }
}

# ---- Build ILP ----
# Slack weighting normalized by mean demand so coefficients stay O(10) and the
# solver avoids numerical instability. big_M = 10 → slacks 10× a corridor.
mean_W <- mean(W[lower.tri(W) & W > 0])
big_M  <- 10

cat("Building model...\n")
t0 <- Sys.time()

model <- MIPModel() %>%
  add_variable(x[c], c = 1:N_cand, type = "binary") %>%
  add_variable(slack[i, j], i = 1:n_nodes, j = 1:n_nodes, i < j, type = "binary")

# Transfer indicator u[t] per viable triple (only if any exist)
if (n_triples > 0L) {
  model <- model %>%
    add_variable(u[t], t = 1:n_triples, type = "binary") %>%
    # u[t] fires only if a selected corridor (or rail) serves leg 1 ...
    add_constraint(
      u[t] <= sum_expr(leg1_coef[t, c] * x[c], c = 1:N_cand) + triple_rail1[t],
      t = 1:n_triples
    ) %>%
    # ... and another serves leg 2
    add_constraint(
      u[t] <= sum_expr(leg2_coef[t, c] * x[c], c = 1:N_cand) + triple_rail2[t],
      t = 1:n_triples
    )
}

# Pair coverage: direct OR a viable transfer OR slack ≥ 1 (minus rail direct).
if (n_triples > 0L) {
  model <- model %>%
    add_constraint(
      sum_expr(direct_serves[c, i, j] * x[c], c = 1:N_cand) +
        sum_expr(serves[t, i, j] * u[t], t = 1:n_triples) +
        slack[i, j] >= 1 - rail_direct[i, j],
      i = 1:n_nodes, j = 1:n_nodes, i < j
    )
} else {
  model <- model %>%
    add_constraint(
      sum_expr(direct_serves[c, i, j] * x[c], c = 1:N_cand) +
        slack[i, j] >= 1 - rail_direct[i, j],
      i = 1:n_nodes, j = 1:n_nodes, i < j
    )
}

model <- model %>%
  # Rightsizing: Σ_c (touches[c,i] - tolerance × D_i) × x_c ≤ 0
  add_constraint(
    sum_expr((touches[c, i] - tolerance * D_share[i]) * x[c], c = 1:N_cand) <= 0,
    i = 1:n_nodes
  ) %>%
  set_objective(
    sum_expr(x[c], c = 1:N_cand) +
      big_M * sum_expr((W[i, j] / mean_W) * slack[i, j],
                       i = 1:n_nodes, j = 1:n_nodes, i < j),
    "min"
  )

cat(sprintf("Model built in %.1f s. Solving with HiGHS...\n",
            as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")))

t1 <- Sys.time()
result <- solve_model(model, with_ROI(solver = "highs", verbose = TRUE))
cat(sprintf("Solver: %s, objective = %.0f, solved in %.1f s\n",
            solver_status(result),
            objective_value(result),
            as.numeric(Sys.time() - t1, units = "secs")))

# ---- Extract solution ----
selected_x <- get_solution(result, x[c]) %>%
  filter(value > 0.5) %>%
  pull(c)

slack_solution <- get_solution(result, slack[i, j]) %>%
  filter(value > 0.5) %>%
  mutate(cell_a = node_info$cell_id[i],
         cell_b = node_info$cell_id[j])

cat(sprintf("\nILP selected %d bus corridors (down from greedy's %d)\n",
            length(selected_x),
            sum(vapply(selected_corridors, function(c) c$type == "bus", logical(1)))))
cat(sprintf("Pairs with slack (impossible to cover under these constraints): %d\n",
            nrow(slack_solution)))
if (nrow(slack_solution) > 0) {
  cat("  Slacks:\n"); print(slack_solution %>% select(cell_a, cell_b))
}

# ---- Replace selected_corridors: rail + ILP-selected bus ----
rail_only <- Filter(function(sc) sc$type == "rail", selected_corridors)

bus_selected <- vector("list", length(selected_x))
for (k in seq_along(selected_x)) {
  sel <- candidates[[selected_x[k]]]
  sel$type  <- "bus"
  sel$label <- sprintf("Bus %d", k)
  # Demand this corridor serves DIRECTLY (sum of W over node-pairs both on it)
  sq  <- sel$sequence
  dem <- 0
  if (length(sq) >= 2L) {
    for (a in seq_len(length(sq) - 1L)) for (b in (a + 1L):length(sq)) {
      dem <- dem + W[sq[a], sq[b]]
    }
  }
  sel$marginal_demand <- dem
  bus_selected[[k]]   <- sel
}

selected_corridors <- c(rail_only, bus_selected)

# Recompute final state using the ILP solution
st  <- compute_service(selected_corridors, transfer_pen, n_full, n_nodes)
pen <- compute_penalty(st$service, W, T_node_min,
                       quality_threshold, unreachable_quality)
state <- list(
  service       = st$service,
  direct        = st$direct,
  penalty_total = pen$total,
  quality       = pen$quality,
  per_pair      = pen$per_pair,
  n_over        = pen$n_over,
  n_unreach     = pen$n_unreach
)

# ---- Rightsizing audit ----
if (length(selected_x) > 0L) {
  service_counts <- colSums(touches[selected_x, , drop = FALSE])
  total_bus      <- length(selected_x)
  service_share  <- service_counts / total_bus
} else {
  service_share <- rep(0, n_nodes)
}

rightsize_df <- data.frame(
  cell_id       = node_info$cell_id,
  demand_share  = round(D_share, 3),
  service_share = round(service_share, 3),
  ratio         = round(service_share / pmax(D_share, 1e-9), 2),
  cap           = round(tolerance * D_share, 3),
  ok            = service_share <= tolerance * D_share + 1e-6
)
cat(sprintf("\nRightsizing audit (S_i / D_i ≤ %.1f):\n", tolerance))
print(rightsize_df)
```

### Prune redundant routes

A route is **redundant** if removing it leaves *every* node-pair's best service
time unchanged — the rest of the network already serves all of that route's
pairs at least as fast. The ILP can keep redundant routes purely to inflate the
corridor count `N`, which loosens the rightsizing cap `n_i / N ≤ tol × D_i` for
heavily-used nodes. Dropping them only relaxes rightsizing (which we accept) and
**provably cannot slow any trip or strand any pair**.

This iteratively drops redundant routes. Note a route whose stop-set is a
*subset* of another's is NOT automatically redundant — if it serves an internal
pair faster than the longer route's detour through that pair, it's genuinely
needed and is kept.

```{r prune-subset-routes}
n_before_prune <- sum(vapply(selected_corridors, function(c) c$type == "bus", logical(1)))

repeat {
  bus_idx     <- which(vapply(selected_corridors, function(c) c$type == "bus", logical(1)))
  dropped_one <- FALSE
  for (b in bus_idx) {
    trial    <- selected_corridors[-b]
    st_trial <- compute_service(trial, transfer_pen, n_full, n_nodes)
    lt       <- lower.tri(state$service)
    # Does removing this route make ANY pair strictly slower (incl. → unreachable)?
    worse <- st_trial$service[lt] > state$service[lt] + 1e-9
    if (!any(worse, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      cat(sprintf("Dropping redundant route %s [%s]\n",
                  selected_corridors[[b]]$label,
                  paste(node_info$cell_id[selected_corridors[[b]]$sequence],
                        collapse = " → ")))
      selected_corridors <- trial
      st  <- st_trial
      pen <- compute_penalty(st$service, W, T_node_min,
                             quality_threshold, unreachable_quality)
      state <- list(service = st$service, direct = st$direct,
                    penalty_total = pen$total, quality = pen$quality,
                    per_pair = pen$per_pair, n_over = pen$n_over,
                    n_unreach = pen$n_unreach)
      dropped_one <- TRUE
      break
    }
  }
  if (!dropped_one) break
}

# Re-label bus corridors sequentially after the drops
bus_ctr <- 0L
for (s in seq_along(selected_corridors)) {
  if (selected_corridors[[s]]$type == "bus") {
    bus_ctr <- bus_ctr + 1L
    selected_corridors[[s]]$label <- sprintf("Bus %d", bus_ctr)
  }
}

n_bus_after <- sum(vapply(selected_corridors, function(c) c$type == "bus", logical(1)))
cat(sprintf("\nRedundant-route prune: %d → %d bus corridors. Over threshold: %d. Unreachable: %d. (No trip slowed, by construction.)\n",
            n_before_prune, n_bus_after, state$n_over, state$n_unreach))
```

### Selected corridors as a table

```{r selected-table}
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a) || is.na(a)) b else a

selected_df <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(selected_corridors), function(s) {
  c <- selected_corridors[[s]]
  data.frame(
    rank             = s,
    type             = c$type,
    label            = c$label,
    n_nodes          = length(c$sequence),
    n_transfer_stops = c$n_transfer_stops %||% 0L,
    path_length_min  = c$path_length_min  %||% NA_real_,
    travel_time_min  = c$travel_time_min  %||%
                        (if (length(c$cum_t) > 0L) tail(c$cum_t, 1) else NA_real_),
    detour_ratio     = c$detour_ratio     %||% NA_real_,
    marginal_demand  = c$marginal_demand,
    sequence_cells   = paste(node_info$cell_id[c$sequence], collapse = " → ")
  )
}))
selected_df
```
